A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VisRAG and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The comparison includes Appendices A–F in v1 and A–I in v2, with retained and relocated material identifiable.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval and generation experiments on six VQA-derived datasets, training-data and document-length analyses, and appendix experiments comparing parsing methods.

after.justification: V2 reports revised retrieval and generation results plus new fusion comparisons, larger-context experiments, latency measurements, and text-only retrieval evaluations.

M1.justification: The VLM dual encoder, position-weighted pooling, InfoNCE objective, page concatenation, weighted selection, and direct multi-image generation remain unchanged in Section 3.2. Evaluating Qwen2-VL does not introduce a new generation procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds SciFact, NFCorpus, and Scidocs from BEIR, extending evaluation from visual-document question answering to text-only document retrieval using rendered screenshots. The original six VQA datasets and training sources remain; their changed evaluation sample counts are protocol changes.

E2.justification: Appendix G adds MiniCPM (OCR) plus SigLIP combined through reciprocal rank fusion in both training regimes, and Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct to generation comparisons. Existing comparators remain. ColPali's revised training data changes its evaluation setting rather than comparator membership.

E3.justification: Query filtering switches from Llama-3-8B-Instruct to GPT-4o with a revised prompt. Table 1 reduces evaluation questions from 26,230 to 3,607, including ChartQA from 718 to 63, while listed training counts and corpus sizes remain unchanged. ColPali is now trained on the authors' dataset rather than evaluated with its original training setup. New experiments introduce top-6/top-10 contexts, latency measurement protocols, and BEIR evaluation using NDCG@10.

E4.justification: Appendix G tests whether combining separate text and image retrievers matches unified VLM retrieval, and extends context sensitivity beyond three retrieved pages to six and ten, exposing degradation. Appendix H adds an offline/online latency breakdown. Existing training-data, document-length, and parsing analyses remain with revised results; the two case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests for its experiments. The new results also use point estimates; percentages relative to Oracle are performance ratios, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 2, 3, 5, and 6 and the performance plots change extensively under revised filtering. For example, average out-of-domain VisRAG-Ret versus NV-Embed-v2 MRR@10 changes from 63.96 versus 63.46 to 71.49 versus 75.24, reversing their ranking. Tables 10–13 add fusion, Qwen2-VL, larger-context, latency, and BEIR results. These are not same-setting performance gains. Table 12's 312 versus 121 ms implies about 61% savings, inconsistent with the accompanying 58% statement.

T1.justification: The retrieval and generation definitions and Equations 1–6 are unchanged. Neither the new experiments nor the appended discussions introduce a theorem, proof, substantive derivation, or revised formal assumption.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a parsing-free VLM retrieval and generation pipeline. The abstract and introduction revise the claimed end-to-end improvement from 25–39% to 20–40%, and the introduction broadens the increasing-context benefit from GPT-4o specifically to multi-image VLMs.

C2.justification: V2 qualifies document-subset superiority as holding on most subsets and revises the training-efficiency discussion to acknowledge trailing NV-Embed-v2. It attributes multi-page reasoning to multi-image pretraining and the fusion comparison to unified multimodal understanding. Appendices add qualifications about residual context-dependent queries and degradation with many retrieved pages, alongside an interpretation supporting text-only applicability.

D1.justification: New reproducibility details include the latency experiment's A100 40GB GPU, batch size one, and single-core Xeon CPU, plus BEIR screenshot dimensions, font, margins, and spacing. V2 also supplies the revised filtering prompt and specifies using ColPali's official code and hyperparameters. Core training details, generation prompts, and the code/data access statement remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds focused coverage of the DocOwl series, UReader, and TextMonkey for OCR-free document understanding. New experiments introduce RRF and BEIR citations, while the Llama 3 model-card reference is removed. The positioning relative to DSE and ColPali remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted rewrites to the introduction, experimental setup, and results discussion, retitles Appendix D, appends Sections G–I, and adds acknowledgments and the ICLR 2025 publication header. The main narrative structure and method exposition remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 10–13, restructures Table 1's filtering columns, and removes ColPali's training-dataset markers from Table 2. Performance plots receive revised curves, scales, and local placement changes. The overall layout, method diagram, and existing case-study displays are retained.

improvement.justification: Training ColPali on shared data and adding fusion controls, larger-context tests, latency measurements, and text-only evaluation strengthen the empirical assessment and clarify failure conditions beyond v1. These benefits are tempered by the sharply smaller filtered evaluation sets without quantified filtering validation or uncertainty estimates, and the new latency arithmetic inconsistency. The evidence supports a useful but limited overall improvement.
